classification.difficultyReason: Read three scale positions and convert the probabilities into colour counts on a ten-sector response diagram.

inlines.text: A fair spinner is split into 10 sections that are either red, blue or green.
The probability of the spinner landing on each colour is shown on the scale.
Complete the diagram to show what the spinner might look like.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14, scale to the left of the spinner
spec.description: Eleven ticks; endpoints 0 and 1; downward arrows labelled B, R and G at the first, third and sixth interior ticks.
spec.mathematics: P(B)=1/10, P(R)=3/10, P(G)=6/10. These interior numbers are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The category positions are supplied question givens.

spec.description: Uncoloured circular response diagram with ten equal sectors and a boundary pointing vertically upward.
spec.mathematics: Ten sectors of 36 degrees each. The angle is construction data, not a printed measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: Approved editorial decision: source colouring is solution-only; students receive an uncoloured partition.

answer.short: 1 blue section, 3 red sections and 6 green sections.
answer.worked:
The scale gives $P(\text{blue})=\frac{1}{10}$, $P(\text{red})=\frac{3}{10}$ and $P(\text{green})=\frac{6}{10}$.

With 10 equally likely sections, the favourable outcomes are 1 blue section, 3 red sections and 6 green sections. Any arrangement with these counts is correct.

spec.description: Clockwise from the vertical top boundary: six green sectors, three red sectors and one blue sector.
spec.mathematics: 6/10 green, 3/10 red and 1/10 blue; ten equal 36-degree sectors.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graphical answer retained only in the solution.
